Its Hifil causative adds the dimension of placing others — appointing a priest, erecting a pillar, establishing a decree. The root is deeply pan-Semitic: Arabic amada means to prop up or support, Ethiopic preserves it in the noun 'pillar' (amud), and Aramaic ammuda carries the same architectural sense. Across translations, the range is striking: Korean distinguishes seoda (stand) from gyeondida (endure) and meomchuda (stop), while Spanish separates pararse from permanecer and establecer."
